NP Size (nm): ~60–80 nm (core MNP-MSN); ~110 nm after PF-127 coating
PEG Details: Pluronic F-127 COOH-modified via succinic anhydride
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 10 mg NPs in 5 mL PBS; 250 µL EDC + 250 µL NHS; 100 µL Tf (1 mg/mL)
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Not reported; DOX loading ~22.6%
Characterization Method: FTIR, TEM, VSM, drug release
Key Finding / Notes: Activate COOH on PF-127-coated MSN with EDC/NHS 4h RT. Add Tf dropwise, incubate 4°C overnight. Centrifuge, wash, lyophilize.

PEG Details: Carboxylated Pluronic F127 + P123, TMOS silica shell
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Equal EDC/NHS (0.25 M) to NPs; 130 µg Tf in PBS
Conjugation Efficiency (%): BCA: slight Tf loss during process; EE 95.7%
Characterization Method: DLS (~90 nm, PDI 0.23), TEM, BCA, zeta
Key Finding / Notes: Add 0.25 M EDC+NHS to NPs, stir 15 min RT. Add 130 µg Tf in PBS, incubate overnight. Ultracentrifuge 93,000g 30 min to separate unbound Tf.

PEG Details: NH2-MSN coated with pH-sensitive polymer
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Tf conjugated to polymer-coated MSN surface via amide bond
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced uptake in MIA PaCa-2 vs non-targeted
Characterization Method: DLS, FTIR, TEM, cytotoxicity, cellular uptake
Key Finding / Notes: Amine-functionalized MSN coated with chitosan or PLGA. Tf conjugated via EDC/NHS to enable receptor-mediated uptake. Optimized pore size 2.5-5.2 nm for gemcitabine loading.

PEG Details: 8arm-PEG-COOH (MW 10 kDa) conjugated to DHA
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 50 mg PEG-conjugate in 10 mL PBS; EDC 4 mg + NHS 6 mg; 8 mg Tf in 5 mL PBS
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Drug loading ~10 wt%; NP size ~147 nm
Characterization Method: NMR, DLS, cytotoxicity (CCK-8), in vivo tumor growth
Key Finding / Notes: Dissolve 50 mg PEG-conjugate in 10 mL PBS. Add EDC(4mg)+NHS(6mg), stir RT 15 min. Add 8 mg Tf in 5 mL PBS, stir RT 6h. Dialyze MWCO 30kDa against PBS 12h. Lyophilize.

PEG Details: Tf grafted via redox-cleavable disulfide bonds to MSN surface
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Tf serves as both capping agent and targeting ligand
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Redox-responsive release; glutathione triggers Tf detachment
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, BET, drug release, cellular uptake
Key Finding / Notes: Alternative to EDC/NHS: Tf grafted via disulfide bonds. Dual function as cap + targeting ligand. GSH-triggered release in tumor microenvironment.

PEG Details: APTS amine surface → SM(PEG)8 linker → terminal maleimide
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): NP:Tf 1:1 mass ratio; TCEP 1:1 molar to Tf
Incubation Time (h): TCEP 5 min; coupling 2h at 400 rpm shaking; quench with β-mercaptoethanol (1 mM) 5 min
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Uptake pathway depends on PEG architecture
Characterization Method: DLS, zeta, fluorescence microscopy, flow cytometry, pathway analysis
Key Finding / Notes: SiNP-NH2 (APTS) → react with SM(PEG)8 for PEG-Maleimide surface. Thiolate Tf with TCEP (1:1, 5 min). Immediately add NP-PEG-Mal to Tf-SH (1:1 mass), react 2h RT 400 rpm. Quench β-mercaptoethanol 1 mM 5 min. Wash 4× PBS. Store 4°C.

PEG Details: Tf functionalized with sulfo-SMCC (maleimide); payload thiolated with Traut's
Activation Agent: Sulfo-SMCC on Tf; Traut's on payload
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Optimized: 1:1 Tf:sulfo-SMCC; Traut's at 1:1 amine ratio, 500 µM protein, 0°C, 12h
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 1:1 conjugate confirmed by mass spectrometry
Characterization Method: ESI-MS, SDS-PAGE, activity assays
Key Finding / Notes: Classical Tf conjugation: derivatize Tf Lys with sulfo-SMCC (introduces maleimide). Thiolate payload with Traut's (1:1, 0°C, 12h, pH 8.0). React immediately. WARNING: Traut's can reduce Tf disulfides at high pH — use low reagent conc and 0°C.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal micelles for post-insertion
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Tf thiolated 1:5 Tf:Traut; DSPE-PEG-Mal at 0.1 mol% of total lipid
Incubation Time (h): Thiolation → coupling → post-insertion; total several hours
Conjugation Efficiency (%): DOX EE 95%; size ~130 nm
Characterization Method: DLS, HPLC (EE), FBS stability, cellular uptake, cytotoxicity
Key Finding / Notes: Post-insertion for dual Tf/TAT liposome: thiolate Tf (Traut 1:5 RT). Couple Tf-SH to DSPE-PEG2000-Mal micelles. Post-insert into preformed DOX liposomes. IC50 decreased 68.7% vs plain liposome.

PEG Details: Mal-mPEG2000-DSPE conjugate post-inserted
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Lipid-to-Tf-PEG conjugate 100:1 molar ratio
Characterization Method: DLS, PDI, EE
Key Finding / Notes: Tf thiolated with Traut's → coupled to Mal-mPEG2000-DSPE → post-inserted into LP-ERN at 100:1 lipid:conjugate, 37°C, 30 min. Neither uniformity nor EE compromised.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Maleimide incorporated; post-insertion coupling
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 1 mol% DSPE-PEG-Mal; antibody:DSPE 1:1; Traut 3:1
Conjugation Efficiency (%): >90% DSPE-PEG-Mal retained (Ellman's); targeting confirmed by fluorescence
Characterization Method: Ellman's test, DLS, fluorescence microscopy
Key Finding / Notes: Thermal equilibration: add DSPE-PEG-Mal (25 mg/mL in DMSO) at 1 mol%, incubate 55°C 1h. Thiolate protein (Traut 3:1, 1h). Add at 1:1 DSPE:protein. Couple overnight 4°C. Quench β-mercaptoethanol 15 min.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG-Maleimide (0.015 µmol) incorporated during liposome formation
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): mAb:Traut 1:40; phospholipid:mAb 100:1 to 400:1; ~10% coupling efficiency; optimal ~30 Ab/liposome
Buffer: 0.15 M Na-borate + 0.1 mM EDTA (thiolation); 0.1 M Na-phosphate (coupling)
Conjugation Efficiency (%): ~10% coupling efficiency; 30 Ab/liposome optimal for brain delivery
Characterization Method: Ellman's (avg 1 thiol/mAb), Sephadex CL-4B column, radiolabeling, pharmacokinetics
Key Finding / Notes: Landmark BBB study: thiolate OX26 mAb (Traut 1:40, borate pH 8.5, 60 min RT). Exchange to phosphate pH 8.0. React immediately with DSPE-PEG-Mal liposomes overnight RT. Separate on Sephadex CL-4B. Coupling not affected by mAb conc at 100-400:1 lipid:mAb.

PEG Details: DSPC:DSPE-PEG2000:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal at 4:1:0.2 molar
Activation Agent: Thiol-maleimide (no EDC needed for Ab coupling)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Ab:DSPE-PEG-Mal 1:10 molar ratio
Incubation Time (h): 4h at 4°C; ultracentrifuge 55,000 rpm 1h to remove unbound
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Functional targeting confirmed
Characterization Method: DLS, SDS-PAGE, Western blot, ultracentrifugation
Key Finding / Notes: DSPC:DSPE-PEG2000:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal at 4:1:0.2. Mix Ab with liposomes at 1:10 Ab:DSPE-PEG-Mal, 4°C, 4h continuous stirring. Ultracentrifuge 55,000 rpm 4°C 1h to remove unconjugated Ab. (Note: this is Mal-thiol, listed under EDC/NHS section as closest liposome-Ab protocol.)

PEG Details: Direct PLGA terminal -COOH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): EDC 20× molar excess to PLGA-COOH; Tf 2× molar excess; target ~100 Tf/NP
Conjugation Efficiency (%): CE measured by BCA (supernatant method)
Characterization Method: DLS, BCA, zeta, SRB cytotoxicity, SDS-PAGE
Key Finding / Notes: Activate PLGA-COOH with EDC (20× excess), agitate RT 30 min. Add Tf (2× excess). Agitate 1h RT. Centrifuge, resuspend in water. Quantify unbound Tf by BCA.

PEG Details: PLGA 50:50 (MW 30-60 kDa) terminal -COOH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): EDC/NHS to activate PLGA-COOH; Tf added for amide bond
Conjugation Efficiency (%): EE 86.2%, DL 7.8%; size 199.5 nm; zeta -17.4 mV
Characterization Method: TEM, SEM, FTIR, DLS, zeta, in vivo brain distribution (IN delivery)
Key Finding / Notes: Double emulsification → PLGA NPs → EDC/NHS coupling with Tf. Confirmed Tf coating by TEM/SEM/FTIR. Enhanced brain uptake via intranasal delivery in rats.

PEG Details: Carboxymethyl chitosan (CMC) coating provides -COOH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 150 mg NPs in 10 mL NaCl (0.5 M, pH 5.5); EDC 2 mM; NHS 5 mM
Incubation Time (h): 15 min activation; quench with 20 mM 2-mercaptoethanol; centrifuge 1000 rpm 10 min 4°C; then add Tf
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced PDT efficacy in A549 cells
Characterization Method: SEM, DLS, FTIR, fluorescence, AO/EB apoptosis staining
Key Finding / Notes: Activate CMC-COOH on NP surface: EDC 2 mM + NHS 5 mM in NaCl pH 5.5, 15 min RT. Quench with 2-mercaptoethanol (20 mM). Centrifuge (1000 rpm, 10 min, 4°C). Add Tf for amide bond.

PEG Details: PEG conjugated to PLGA; Tf (oxalate variant) attached
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): PLGA-PEG-COOH NPs; Tf conjugated to terminal COOH via EDC/NHS
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 3-fold decrease in IC50 for oxalate Tf vs native Tf
Characterization Method: MTS assay, drug release, scaffold incorporation
Key Finding / Notes: PLGA-PEG-Tf NPs incorporated into 3D PLGA scaffolds. Oxalate Tf variant showed greater potency than native Tf — first use of Tf variant for NP delivery in scaffolds.

PEG Details: Tf adsorbed onto PLGA-PEG NP surface (non-covalent)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Tf incubated with preformed PLGA NPs; adsorption-based
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced uptake in MCF-7 and U-87 cells
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, zeta, drug release, cytotoxicity, cellular uptake
Key Finding / Notes: Non-covalent approach: Tf physically adsorbed onto PLGA surface. Simpler than EDC/NHS but less stable. Included as comparison — Tf adsorption is common alternative to covalent conjugation for PLGA.

PEG Details: MBS-DOPE lipid conjugate; DSPE-PEG for stealth
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Tf thiolated in HEPES pH 8 with 5× Traut's; Tf-SH mixed with MB-DOPE micelles at 1:10 protein:lipid molar
Incubation Time (h): 1h thiolation + 1h Tf-lipid coupling + 1h post-insertion into PLGA NP
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Drug loading 36.3 ± 3.4%; zeta -18.9 mV; IC50 0.77-1.21 nM (Tf-NP) vs 1.90-3.41 nM (non-targeted)
Characterization Method: DLS, zeta, HPLC, aromatase inhibition (SKBR-3 cells)
Key Finding / Notes: Lipid-coated PLGA method: (1) Synthesize MB-DOPE (MBS + DOPE in CHCl3 + TEA, overnight RT). (2) Form micelles. (3) Thiolate Tf (5× Traut's, HEPES pH 8). (4) Mix Tf-SH with MB-DOPE micelles 1:10 protein:lipid, 37°C, 1h. (5) Post-insert Tf-DOPE into drug-loaded PLGA NPs, 37°C, 1h.

PEG Details: PLGA-PEG-Maleimide NPs with maleimide surface
Activation Agent: TCEP (100× excess to reduce Ab disulfides)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): TCEP 100× to Ab; ~4 free thiols/Ab; Low loading: 192 Ab/NP; High loading: 1063 Ab/NP
Incubation Time (h): Overnight thiolation; coupling time not specified
Conjugation Efficiency (%): High loading: 1063 ± 97 Ab/NP (TCEP method, best); Ellman's confirmed 4 thiols/Ab
Characterization Method: Ellman's assay, SDS-PAGE, ELISA, DLS, NP tracking
Key Finding / Notes: NOTE: Uses anti-FZD7 Ab not Tf, but protocol directly applicable to Tf-maleimide conjugation on PLGA-PEG-Mal. TCEP 100× to reduce disulfides → 4 free thiols. React with NP-PEG-Mal in PBS+EDTA. Most efficient method tested. (Closest verified Mal-thiol PLGA protocol.)

PEG Details: PEG-maleimide
Conjugation Efficiency (%): full-length antibodies: 7-15%, f(ab')2 fragments: 26-47%
Characterization Method: BCA protein assay
Key Finding / Notes: Directional antibody fragments (f(ab′)₂) gave higher conjugation efficiency and greater immune cell targeting than full IgG on PLGA NPs.

PEG Details: APTES
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): ~262.5 ng antibody per 3 mg NP
Characterization Method: TEM, ζ-potential, fluorescence assay
Key Finding / Notes: Silica NPs (~45 nm) were amine-functionalized (APTES) and then covalently linked to EGFR antibodies using EDC/NHS chemistry in saline.

PEG Details: Two-step PEGylation: Mal-PEG5k-NH2 for surface amine; Mal-PEG5k-SCM for terminal maleimide
Activation Agent: TCEP (thiol reduction of TRC105); Ellman's to quantify –SH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 100 nmol –SH on mSiO2-SH; 2 mg Mal-PEG5k-NH2 (400 nmol) for 1st PEGylation; TRC105-SH added at 200 µg per 1 mg NPs
Incubation Time (h): 1st PEGylation overnight; TRC105 coupling 2 h RT
Conjugation Efficiency (%): ~17.5% ID/g tumor at 24 h PET; specific tumor uptake confirmed vs IgG control
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, Ellman's assay, radio-PET (64Cu-NOTA), biodistribution, blocking studies
Key Finding / Notes: Thiolate mSiO2-SH with MPS at 86–90 °C ethanol. PEGylate with Mal-PEG5k-NH2 overnight RT. Install NOTA then Mal-PEG5k-SCM surface. Reduce TRC105 disulfides with TCEP, react with NP-PEG-Mal 2 h RT.

PEG Details: PEI cross-linked with DSP; Maleimide-PEG (5 kDa)-NHS installed on PEI at 1:1 mass ratio
Activation Agent: Traut's reagent (50-fold molar excess to trastuzumab, pH 8.0, 2 h)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): MSNP-PEI at 4:1 mass ratio PEI; Mal-PEG-NHS 1:1 mass to MSNP-PEI; Trastuzumab-SH added to MSNP-PEI-PEG
Buffer: Phosphate pH 8.0 (thiolation); PBS pH 7.2 (PEG + Ab coupling)
Incubation Time (h): 2 h PEG coupling; Traut's thiolation 2 h; Ab coupling overnight 4 °C
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Maintained targeting over 9-month lyophilized storage; HER2+ cell uptake confirmed by flow cytometry
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, Zeta, BCA protein quantification, flow cytometry, lyophilization stability
Key Finding / Notes: Coat MSNP (50 nm) with branched PEI (4:1) in ethanol 3 h. Cross-link with DSP 40 min. Conjugate Mal-PEG5k-NHS (1:1) in PBS pH 7.2, 2 h. Thiolate trastuzumab with Traut's 50×, pH 8.0, 2 h. React trastuzumab-SH with MSNP-PEI-PEG overnight 4 °C.

PEG Details: PEG2000-COOH tethered to ORMOSIL surface; provides spacer and carboxyl for Ab coupling
Activation Agent: EDC + Sulfo-NHS (standard carbodiimide activation of PEG-COOH)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): ORMOSIL-PEG-COOH 1 mg; EDC 0.4 mg + Sulfo-NHS 0.6 mg; cetuximab added at ~5 µg Ab per mg NP
Incubation Time (h): 15 min activation; 2 h coupling at RT
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced uptake in EGFR+ Panc-1 cells vs non-targeted; photosensitizer delivery confirmed
Characterization Method: DLS (~30 nm), TEM, Zeta, fluorescence microscopy, cellular uptake (Panc-1, MCF-7)
Key Finding / Notes: Synthesize ORMOSIL (APTS + VPTES) in Aerosol OT/DMSO/water microemulsion. PEGylate surface with PEG2000-COOH. Activate COOH with EDC/Sulfo-NHS (MES pH 6, 15 min). Desalt. Add cetuximab in PBS pH 7.4, 2 h RT. Wash by centrifugation.

PEG Details: Surface thiol (MPS) reacted with Mal-PEG5k-NH2; second Mal-PEG5k-SCM for terminal maleimide for Ab
Activation Agent: TCEP to reduce TRC105 disulfides; Ellman's test to confirm –SH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): mSiO2-SH 100 nmol –SH; Mal-PEG5k-NH2 2 mg (400 nmol); TRC105-SH 200 µg per 1 mg NPs; NP:Ab ~5:1 (w/w)
Incubation Time (h): Thiol-PEG overnight; Ab-maleimide coupling 2 h RT
Conjugation Efficiency (%): ~5 TRC105 per NP (estimated); tumor:muscle uptake ratio >5:1 by PET imaging
Characterization Method: Ellman's assay, DLS (83 nm post-Ab), Zeta, 64Cu-PET, γ-counting biodistribution
Key Finding / Notes: Thiolate mSiO2 with MPS 86-90 °C. PEGylate with Mal-PEG5k-NH2 (100 nmol) overnight RT (consumes all –SH). Install Mal-PEG5k-SCM for second maleimide end. TCEP-reduce TRC105, immediately react with NP-PEG-Mal (2 h RT). Quench with β-mercaptoethanol (1 mM).

PEG Details: APTS surface amine + SM(PEG)8 → terminal maleimide; PEG8 spacer reduces steric hindrance
Activation Agent: TCEP (1:1 molar to Ab Cys, 5 min RT) to expose thiol; SM(PEG)8 at 10× molar excess to NP-NH2
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): NP-NH2 + SM(PEG)8 (10× molar excess, pH 7.4 HEPES, 1 h). Ab-SH (TCEP, 5 min). NP-PEG-Mal + Ab-SH at 1:1 mass ratio.
Incubation Time (h): SM(PEG)8 1 h; TCEP reduction 5 min; Ab coupling 2 h at 400 rpm; quench β-mercaptoethanol 1 mM 5 min
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Receptor-specific uptake confirmed; uptake pathway depends on PEG architecture; >80% Ab activity retained
Characterization Method: DLS, Zeta, fluorescence microscopy, flow cytometry, uptake pathway inhibition (dynasore, MβCD)
Key Finding / Notes: React SiNP-NH2 (APTS) with SM(PEG)8 (10×, HEPES pH 7.4, 1 h RT). Reduce Ab disulfides with TCEP (1:1, 5 min). Immediately add NP-PEG-Mal to Ab-SH (1:1 mass). React 2 h RT 400 rpm. Quench β-mercaptoethanol 1 mM, 5 min. Wash 4× PBS.

PEGylated?: Yes (PEI + NHS-PEG4-N3 for click; EDC/NHS for DBCO labelling of Ab)
PEG Details: PEI-coated MSNP azide-functionalized via NHS-PEG4-N3 + EDC; Ab DBCO-labelled via NHS ester
Activation Agent: NHS ester-PEG4-N3 (1.5 mg per 5 mg NPs in DMSO, borate pH 8.5, 4 h); DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester (10 eq. per Ab, borate pH 8.5, 6 h)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 10 mol eq. DBCO-PEG4-NHS ester per Ab at 1 mg/mL borate pH 8.5; 100 µg DBCO-labelled Ab per 450 µL NPs (10 mg/mL)
Incubation Time (h): NP azide coupling: 4 h; Ab DBCO labelling: 6 h; click conjugation: overnight at RT
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Specific uptake in EGFR+ A431 cells; no uptake in HEK293 (EGFR−); Dox release confirmed in acidic lysosomes
Characterization Method: DLS (~130 nm, PDI <0.2), Zeta, TEM, confocal microscopy, flow cytometry, MTT, Zeba spin cleanup
Key Finding / Notes: Coat MSNP with 0.75% PEI (pH 7, 1:1, 3 h, magnetic stir). Add NHS-PEG4-N3 (1.5 mg in DMSO) to PEI-MSNP in borate pH 8.5, stir 4 h. Centrifuge. Label Ab with DBCO-PEG4-NHS (10 eq., borate pH 8.5, 6 h). Purify on Zeba 40K. Mix DBCO-Ab (100 µg) with N3-NP (450 µL × 10 mg/mL), overnight RT. Centrifuge, wash.

PEG Details: Surface –COOH groups intrinsic to carboxylated silica; direct EDC/NHS coupling of Ab
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 1 mg SiO2-COOH NPs; EDC 0.4 mg + Sulfo-NHS 1.1 mg in MES pH 6.0; cetuximab 25 µg in PBS pH 7.4
Incubation Time (h): 30 min activation; 1–2 h coupling; quench hydroxylamine 10 min
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 1–20% coupling efficiency typical for EDC/NHS (random amine coupling); targeting confirmed by cell assay
Characterization Method: DLS, Zeta, BCA assay, SDS-PAGE, flow cytometry, cellular uptake (EGFR+ cancer cells)
Key Finding / Notes: Dissolve cetuximab 1 mg/mL in MES pH 6.0. Add EDC (0.4 mg) + Sulfo-NHS (1.1 mg). Incubate 30 min RT. Transfer activated Ab to carboxylated SiNP in PBS pH 7.4. React 1–2 h RT on rotator. Quench with hydroxylamine (10 mM final). Wash 3× PBS by centrifugation.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal provides both stealth PEG and reactive maleimide at lipid bilayer surface
Activation Agent: Traut's reagent (protein:Traut 3:1 molar, pH 7–8, 1 h RT)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DSPE-PEG2000-Mal 0.5–1 mol% of total lipid; trastuzumab-SH added at 1:1 Ab:DSPE-PEG-Mal molar ratio
Incubation Time (h): Traut's thiolation 1 h RT; maleimide coupling overnight 4 °C
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced cytotoxicity vs plain liposomes in HER2+ SKBR-3 cells; EE ~90% for rapamycin
Characterization Method: DLS, PDI, Zeta, BCA, Ellman's assay, MTT cytotoxicity (SKBR-3 cells), confocal
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare liposomes by thin-film hydration/extrusion (DSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal at 56:39:0.5–1 mol ratio). Thiolate trastuzumab with Traut's 3:1 molar, 1 h RT. React trastuzumab-SH with DSPE-PEG-Mal liposomes overnight 4 °C. Wash unbound Ab by ultrafiltration (MWCO 100 kDa).

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal provides PEG stealth layer and terminal maleimide for site-specific Ab coupling
Activation Agent: Traut's reagent (cetuximab:Traut 3:1 molar, pH 8.0, 1 h RT) to introduce –SH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DSPE-PEG2000-Mal 1 mol% total lipid; cetuximab-SH at 1:1 molar ratio to DSPE-PEG-Mal; ~10–30 Ab/liposome optimal
Incubation Time (h): 1 h thiolation RT + overnight coupling at 4 °C
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Selective uptake in EGFR+ A431 cells; 5-FU delivery enhanced vs non-targeted; ~30 Ab/liposome
Characterization Method: DLS, Zeta, Ellman's, SDS-PAGE, cellular uptake (A431), cytotoxicity (5-FU payload)
Key Finding / Notes: Hydrate lipid film (DSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal). Extrude through 100 nm membrane. Thiolate cetuximab (Traut's 3:1, pH 8.0, 1 h). Add cetuximab-SH to liposomes at 1:1 Ab:DSPE-PEG-Mal, incubate overnight 4 °C. Remove unbound Ab by gel filtration (Sephadex CL-4B) or ultrafiltration.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000 (stealth) + DSPE-PEG2000-Mal (reactive); VHH C-terminal Cys for site-specific coupling
Activation Agent: Engineered C-terminal Cys on VHH; TCEP reduction; NHS activation of maleimide arm
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DSPE-PEG2000-Mal 3 mol% total lipid; VHH-SH added at 5:1 VHH:DSPE-PEG-Mal molar ratio
Incubation Time (h): VHH-SH reduction 30 min; coupling 2 h RT; purify by size exclusion
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Bivalent bispecific VHH-liposomes showed highest affinity to HER2+ cells vs monovalent; 10-fold uptake increase
Characterization Method: DLS, Zeta, BCA, ELISA (HER2 binding), flow cytometry (BT474, SKBR-3), SPR affinity
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare liposome (HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000:DSPE-PEG2000-Mal at 56:38:3:3 mol ratio) by extrusion. Reduce engineered Cys-VHH with TCEP (1:1, 30 min RT). React VHH-SH with Mal-liposomes (5:1 VHH:DSPE-PEG-Mal, PBS 7.4, 2 h RT). Remove free VHH by SEC (Superdex 200).

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG-Maleimide incorporated into bilayer; ~30 Ab/liposome optimal for BBB delivery
Activation Agent: Traut's reagent (mAb:Traut 1:40 mol/mol, borate pH 8.5, 60 min RT)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): mAb:Traut 1:40; phospholipid:mAb 100–400:1; ~10% coupling efficiency; optimal ~30 Ab/liposome; 0.015 µmol DSPE-PEG-Mal
pH: 8.5 (Traut's thiolation in borate); 8.0 (coupling in phosphate buffer)
Buffer: 0.15 M Na-borate + 0.1 mM EDTA (thiolation); 0.1 M Na-phosphate (coupling)
Conjugation Efficiency (%): ~10% coupling efficiency; 30 Ab/liposome optimal; enhanced brain delivery in rats (BBB crossing)
Characterization Method: Ellman's (avg 1 thiol/mAb), Sephadex CL-4B SEC, radiolabeling (3H-cholesterol), pharmacokinetics in rats
Key Finding / Notes: Landmark BBB immunoliposome protocol: thiolate OX26 mAb (Traut's 1:40, borate pH 8.5, 60 min RT). Exchange to phosphate pH 8.0. React with DSPE-PEG-Mal liposomes overnight RT. Separate on Sephadex CL-4B. Coupling efficiency ~10% (1 thiol/mAb avg).

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal added post-formation (55 °C, 1 h thermal equilibration); thiolated trastuzumab coupled overnight 4 °C
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 1 mol% DSPE-PEG-Mal added post-extrusion; trastuzumab-SH at 1:1 molar ratio to DSPE-PEG-Mal; quench β-mercaptoethanol 15 min
Conjugation Efficiency (%): >90% DSPE-PEG-Mal retained (Ellman's); specific targeting of HER2+ cells confirmed by fluorescence
Characterization Method: Ellman's test, DLS, fluorescence microscopy (HER2+ vs HER2− cells)
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare liposomes by thin-film/extrusion (DSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG). Post-insert DSPE-PEG-Mal (25 mg/mL DMSO stock) at 1 mol%, 55 °C, 1 h. Thiolate trastuzumab (Traut's 3:1, 1 h RT). React trastuzumab-SH at 1:1 DSPE:Ab, overnight 4 °C. Quench β-mercaptoethanol (1 mM, 15 min).

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal dissolved as micelles; Cetuximab Fab' thiolated by partial reduction; post-inserted
Activation Agent: 2-MEA (2-mercaptoethylamine, 10 mM) to reduce F(ab')2 → Fab'-SH; 37 °C, 90 min
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Cetuximab IgG → F(ab')2 by pepsin digestion; 2-MEA 10 mM reduces F(ab')2 to Fab'-SH; DSPE-PEG-Mal micelles added at 1:1 Ab:lipid molar ratio; 37 °C 30 min post-insertion
Incubation Time (h): 90 min reduction; Fab'-SH coupling 2 h RT; 37 °C 30 min post-insertion
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Specific binding to EGFR+ UM-SCC1 cells; boron delivery enhanced for BNCT application
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, ELISA, competitive binding, BNCT cell killing assay
Key Finding / Notes: Digest cetuximab with pepsin to obtain F(ab')2. Reduce with 2-MEA (10 mM, 37 °C, 90 min) for Fab'-SH. React Fab'-SH with DSPE-PEG-Mal micelles (1:1, 2 h RT). Post-insert into preformed liposomes (37 °C, 30 min). Remove free Fab' by size exclusion.

PEGylated?: Yes (DSPE-PEG2000-COOH 1 mol% provides carboxyl + PEG stealth)
PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-COOH incorporated at 1 mol%; provides carboxyl end for EDC coupling to Ab amine
Activation Agent: EDC (10-fold molar excess to PEG-COOH) + Sulfo-NHS (25-fold molar excess)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): EDC 10× and Sulfo-NHS 25× molar excess to reactive PEG-COOH (0.11 mM exposed); trastuzumab 1:10 molar ratio (Ab:lipid)
pH: ~6.0 (activation in PBS pH 6); ~7.4 (coupling in PBS pH 7.4)
Incubation Time (h): 15 min activation; quench EDC with 2-mercaptoethanol (20 mM); 2 h coupling
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 20–45% coupling efficiency; risk of inter-liposome crosslinking at high concentrations; dialysis cleanup
Characterization Method: DLS, Zeta, BCA, cellular uptake (HER2+ cells), dialysis cleanup (MWCO <1,000 kDa Float-A-Lyzer)
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare DSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000-COOH liposomes. Activate COOH with EDC (10×) + Sulfo-NHS (25×), PBS pH 6, 15 min. Quench excess EDC with 2-mercaptoethanol (20 mM). Add trastuzumab at 1:10 Ab:lipid molar ratio, PBS pH 7.4, 2 h RT. Dialyze vs PBS (MWCO 300 kDa) to remove unbound Ab. Risk of crosslinking: use dilute conditions.

PEG Details: PLGA-PEG-NHS diblock; NHS end directly couples Ab primary amine in one step
Activation Agent: EDC/NHS co-activation of terminal carboxyl on PLGA-PEG block
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): PLGA-PEG-NHS NPs; anti-TNFR2 Ab or IgG isotype control added at optimized Ab:NP ratio; aqueous PBS
Conjugation Efficiency (%): TNFR2-NPs: 128 ± 2.0 nm (DLS); potent in vivo tumor growth inhibition in MC38 colon cancer; increased CD8+ CTLs
Characterization Method: DLS, PDI, SEM, SDS-PAGE (Ab integrity), flow cytometry, in vivo MC38 mouse model, IHC
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare PLGA-PEG-NHS NPs by solvent injection method. Add anti-TNFR2 Ab (or control IgG) in PBS pH 7.4, incubate 2 h RT. Wash 3× PBS by centrifugation to remove unbound Ab. Characterize by DLS and SDS-PAGE.

PEG Details: PLGA terminal –COOH activated by EDC/Sulfo-NHS; direct Ab coupling via amide bond
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): PLGA-NPs 1 mg/mL; EDC/Sulfo-NHS standard concentrations; cetuximab added at 25 µg per mg NP
Incubation Time (h): 30 min EDC/NHS activation; 2 h Ab coupling
Conjugation Efficiency (%): CE ~40%; size 120 nm; zeta −21 mV; enhanced uptake in U-87MG, SK-Mel 28, SW480 (EGFR+) cells
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, Zeta, BCA, SDS-PAGE, flow cytometry (cellular uptake), apoptosis assay, Western blot (γ-H2AX)
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare TMZ-PLGA-NPs by single emulsion (PLGA 50:50, PVA stabilizer). Activate COOH with EDC + Sulfo-NHS in MES pH 6.0, 30 min RT. Exchange to PBS pH 7.4. Add cetuximab 25 µg per mg NP, stir 2 h RT. Centrifuge, wash 3× PBS.

PEG Details: Terminal PLGA-COOH activated by EDC/NHS; Ab amine forms amide bond on NP surface
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): PLGA-NP 1 mg; EDC/NHS standard concentrations; cetuximab 20–25 µg per mg NP; ~39.8% conjugation efficiency
Conjugation Efficiency (%): CE 39.77 ± 3.4%; size 128.4 ± 3.6 nm; zeta −31.0 ± 0.8 mV; higher EGFR+ cell cytotoxicity vs unconjugated NPs
Characterization Method: DLS, Zeta, BCA (CE), SDS-PAGE, in vitro release (sustained, 25% at pH 5.5/48 h), MTT, cell cycle, apoptosis
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare docetaxel-PLGA NPs by single emulsion solvent evaporation. Activate COOH with EDC/NHS in MES pH 6.0 (30 min). Transfer to PBS pH 7.4. Add cetuximab (~25 µg/mg NP), stir 2 h RT. Centrifuge; wash. Confirm by BCA.

PEG Details: PLGA-PEG-Maleimide NPs synthesized by nanoprecipitation; surface Mal for Ab-SH thioether bond
Activation Agent: TCEP (100-fold molar excess to Ab to reduce disulfides → ~4 free thiols/Ab); 2 mM EDTA in PBS
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): TCEP 100× to Ab; ~4 thiols/Ab by Ellman's; Low loading: 192 Ab/NP; High loading: 1063 ± 97 Ab/NP
Incubation Time (h): Overnight thiolation at 4 °C; RT coupling (time not specified, typically 2–4 h)
Conjugation Efficiency (%): High loading: 1063 ± 97 Ab/NP (TCEP method); Ellman's confirmed ~4 thiols/Ab; ELISA confirmed Ab activity
Characterization Method: Ellman's assay, SDS-PAGE, ELISA, DLS, NP tracking analysis
Key Finding / Notes: Synthesize PLGA-PEG-Mal NPs by nanoprecipitation. Reduce Ab disulfides with TCEP (100×, PBS + 2 mM EDTA, 4 °C overnight). Mix Ab-SH with PLGA-PEG-Mal NPs in PBS + 2 mM EDTA, RT. Purify by centrifugation. Quantify Ab loading by Ellman's assay and ELISA.

PEG Details: PLGA-PEG-Mal diblock; f(ab')2 fragment DTT-reduced to expose thiol in hinge region for site-specific coupling
Activation Agent: IdeS protease (fragment Ab to f(ab')2 + Fc); DTT (10 mM, 2.5 µL per 100 µg Ab) to expose hinge –SH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DTT 2.5 µL of 10 mM per 100 µg Ab; f(ab')2-SH 5–25 µg per 1 mg NPs (8 mg/mL); coupling 2 h 25 °C shaking
Incubation Time (h): DTT reduction (not specified, typ. 30 min); 7 kDa MWCO desalting; 2 h coupling 25 °C
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Maleimide: 99% Ab retained after 5 days (superior stability vs EDC/NHS at 84%); targeting confirmed by flow cytometry
Characterization Method: DLS, SEM, BCA, Zeta, stability assay (5-day incubation), flow cytometry (CD8+ T cells), cell binding
Key Finding / Notes: Cleave Ab with IdeS protease to obtain f(ab')2. Reduce f(ab')2 with DTT (10 mM, 2.5 µL per 100 µg Ab). Desalt on 7 kDa MWCO column. Add f(ab')2-SH (5–25 µg) to PLGA-PEG-Mal NPs (1 mg, 8 mg/mL), 2 h 25 °C shaking. Quantify by BCA. Maleimide method shows superior stability vs EDC/NHS.

PEG Details: Sulfo-SMCC introduces maleimide groups to PLGA-PEG-NH2 NP surface; Ab thiolated with Traut's
Activation Agent: Sulfo-SMCC (NHS ester on NP amine; maleimide for Ab thiol); Traut's reagent (Ab:Traut 1:5, pH 7.4, 1 h)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Sulfo-SMCC 10× molar to NP-NH2; Ab:Traut 1:5 molar ratio; Ab-SH mixed with NP-Mal at 25 µg Ab per mg NP
Incubation Time (h): Sulfo-SMCC 1 h; Traut's thiolation 1 h; maleimide coupling 2 h RT
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced intracellular uptake and cytotoxicity of paclitaxel in CD133+ cancer cells vs non-targeted NPs
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, Zeta, BCA, flow cytometry, MTT cytotoxicity (CD133+ A549 cells)
Key Finding / Notes: Prepare paclitaxel-PLGA-PEG-NH2 NPs by nanoprecipitation. React with sulfo-SMCC (10× molar, PBS pH 7.4, 1 h) to install maleimide. Thiolate anti-CD133 Ab with Traut's (1:5, pH 7.4, 1 h). Desalt on G-25 column. Mix Ab-SH with NP-Mal (25 µg Ab/mg NP, PBS+EDTA, 2 h RT). Purify by centrifugation.

PEG Details: Polyacrylic acid (PAA) brush surface with -COOH
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): GRGDS 0.1 mg/mL; EDC/NHS 1:2.5 molar ratio; 30 min activation in MES pH 6
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 78% increase in efficiency with optimized protocol vs baseline
Characterization Method: In situ FTIR (amide I+II peaks), ellipsometry, AFM
Key Finding / Notes: Optimized EDC/NHS for RGD: MES pH 6 activation 30 min, borate pH 8.0 coupling 16h at 25°C. Temperature and reaction time had greatest impact. EDC/NHS ratio had minor effect. Primary amine on glycine residue is main reactive site.

PEG Details: DOTA carboxylic acid functions on NP surface
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): 5 equiv EDC/HBTU mixture; 6 equiv protected peptide ATWLPPR
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Functional PDT + MRI theranostic NPs confirmed
Characterization Method: TEM, DLS, MRI relaxivity, singlet oxygen, PDT cytotoxicity
Key Finding / Notes: Activate DOTA-COOH on NP with EDC/HBTU (5 equiv) in water/DMSO 10 min. Add protected peptide (6 equiv), stir 18h RT. Evaporate solvents. Deprotect side chains with TFA 2h RT. Wash cycles to remove TFA/DMSO.

PEG Details: Hyaluronic acid (HA) + RGD dual targeting on MSN surface
Activation Agent: EDC/NHS for HA-RGD conjugation to MSN
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): HA and RGD conjugated to GNRs@mSiO2 for dual CD44 + integrin targeting
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Drug loading ~19.8% DOX; pH-enzyme and NIR-triggered release
Characterization Method: FTIR, UV-vis, 1H NMR, DLS, cellular uptake
Key Finding / Notes: Dual-targeted: HA for CD44 receptor + RGD for integrin αvβ3. EDC/NHS used for both conjugations to MSN-NH2 surface. DOX loaded with pH-enzyme sensitive and NIR-triggered release.

PEG Details: MSN-NH2 → Mal-PEG12-NHS crosslinker → MSN-PEGmal
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): RGD-FAM/MSN-PEGmal ratios: 0.32 µmol/mg (high) or 0.16 µmol/mg (low)
Conjugation Efficiency (%): High cluster: 29.1 nmol RGD/mg MSN; Low cluster: 14.5 nmol RGD/mg MSN
Characterization Method: Fluorescence (FAM quantification), DLS, SEM, stem cell adhesion/differentiation
Key Finding / Notes: Two-step: (1) React MSN-NH2 with Mal-PEG12-NHS to form MSN-PEGmal. (2) Conjugate Cys-RGD-FAM to maleimide via thiol-maleimide click. Tune RGD density by adjusting peptide:MSN ratio. PEG12 serves as antifouling spacer.

PEG Details: MSN surface thiol-modified with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): MSN-SH → 2,2'-DTP → activated MSN; then react with Cys-cRGD
Incubation Time (h): Drug loaded in DMF, then peptide conjugated
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Enhanced selectivity: Tf for Panc-1, RGD for BT-549 metastatic cells
Characterization Method: Fluorescence microscopy, flow cytometry, cell proliferation
Key Finding / Notes: Thiol-disulfide method: MSN-SH (via 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane) activated with 2,2'-DTP, load CPT drug in DMF, then react with cRGD peptide. Different from Tf (epoxide method) in same paper — demonstrates ligand-specific chemistry selection.

PEG Details: Stimuli-responsive pNIBIm-AA polymer shell on MSN; RGD conjugated to polymer
Activation Agent: EDC/NHS for polymer graft; peptide via Cys
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): RGD incorporated into polymer shell at varying densities
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Dose-dependent cytotoxicity; enhanced at 40°C vs 37°C
Characterization Method: DLS, TEM, zeta, SBF stability, cell viability (C2C12, BAEC, HepG2)
Key Finding / Notes: Thermo+pH responsive NP: vinyl-MSN coated with pNIBIm-AA-RGD copolymer. RGD provides integrin targeting. DOX release controlled by temperature (LCST) and pH. Dual-stimuli responsive system.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal dissolved in PBS + EDTA + TEA
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DSPE-PEG-Mal (1 mmol) + cRGD (2 mmol, 2× molar excess); in PBS pH 7.2, 0.15 M NaCl, 2 mM EDTA, 2 mmol TEA
Buffer: 0.1 M PBS + 0.15 M NaCl + 2 mM EDTA
Conjugation Efficiency (%): EE >90% apatinib; confirmed by 1H-NMR
Characterization Method: 1H-NMR, DLS, zeta, EE by ultrafiltration, cellular uptake (coumarin-6), in vivo DiR imaging
Key Finding / Notes: Dissolve DSPE-PEG2000-Mal (1 mmol) in PBS pH 7.2 + NaCl + EDTA with TEA. Add 2 equiv cRGD. React under argon, RT, dark, 12h. Dialyze MWCO 1 kDa to remove free cRGD. Then prepare liposomes by thin-film dispersion with cRGD-DSPE-PEG.

PEG Details: MBPE (maleimidobenzoylphosphatidylethanolamine) in liposome; DSPE-PEG2000 post-inserted after cRGD coupling
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): cRGD coupled to MBPE maleimide on preformed liposome surface; then PEG post-inserted
Incubation Time (h): cRGD coupling first, then PEG post-insertion
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Coupling efficiency 98%; DOX EE >98%; zeta -24.85 mV
Characterization Method: DLS, HPLC (coupling efficiency + EE), flow cytometry, competitive binding, pharmacokinetics in rats
Key Finding / Notes: Sequence matters: (1) Prepare liposomes (thin film hydration + extrusion). (2) Load DOX (ammonium sulfate gradient). (3) Couple cRGD to surface MBPE-maleimide via thiol. (4) Post-insert DSPE-PEG2000. PEG inserted AFTER cRGD to avoid steric hindrance blocking maleimide. 98% coupling efficiency.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG-MAL in liposome formulation
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): cRGD:maleimide = 1:10 molar ratio; 1 mg/mL cRGD in 50 mM HEPES pH 6.5
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Functional RGD-LCL confirmed; matrine loaded by pH gradient
Characterization Method: TEM, HPLC (coupling + EE), MTT cytotoxicity, Annexin V apoptosis
Key Finding / Notes: cRGD (1 mg/mL in HEPES pH 6.5) reacted with LCL suspension at 1:10 cRGD:maleimide molar ratio, RT, overnight. Then matrine loaded by pH gradient (inside pH 4.0, outside pH 7.0). Targets αvβ3 integrin on tumor cells + neovasculature.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG-COOH provides terminal carboxyl for amide bond with peptide amine
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DSPE-PEG-COOH activated with EDC/NHS; c(RGD) peptide amine reacts
Conjugation Efficiency (%): RGD-liposomes accumulated at blood clot site; superior to non-targeted
Characterization Method: DLS, in vivo clot targeting, drug release
Key Finding / Notes: Alternative to Mal-thiol for peptide-liposome: use DSPE-PEG-COOH and activate with EDC/NHS to form amide bond with peptide primary amine. Vaidya et al used this for streptokinase-loaded RGD liposomes targeting blood clots.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-COOH terminal carboxyl
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Peptide amine + DSPE-PEG-COOH via amide bond
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Functional targeting confirmed in multiple studies
Characterization Method: DLS, zeta, cellular uptake, in vivo biodistribution
Key Finding / Notes: EDC/NHS approach for peptide-liposome: activate DSPE-PEG-COOH, react with peptide primary amine. Less selective than Mal-thiol (random orientation) but doesn't require Cys-modified peptide. Review describes multiple examples.

PEG Details: DSPE-PEG2000-Mal + DSPE-PEG5000-Mal reacted with thiolated RGD
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): DSPE-PEG-Mal reacted with thiolated RGD; 1-5 mol% DSPE-PEG-RGD incorporated
Conjugation Efficiency (%): MALDI-TOF confirmed quantitative coupling (MW increase ~818.9 Da = RGD-SH)
Characterization Method: MALDI-TOF MS, DLS, zeta, FAM-siRNA uptake by flow cytometry, integrin blocking assay
Key Finding / Notes: MALDI-TOF confirmed quantitative 1:1 DSPE-PEG:RGD coupling. 5 mol% DSPE-PEG-RGD showed highest siRNA delivery to ARPE-19 cells. Integrin blocking (αvβ3, α5β1) reduced but didn't eliminate uptake — multiple integrin subtypes contribute.

PEG Details: PLGA terminal -COOH or surface -COOH groups
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Standard EDC activation of PLGA-COOH; peptide-NH2 reacts to form amide
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Lower efficiency than Mal-thiol for peptides; random orientation
Characterization Method: BCA/fluorescence, DLS, zeta
Key Finding / Notes: Direct EDC/NHS on PLGA: less common for peptides than Mal-thiol because peptides are small and random amide bond orientation is acceptable. Activate PLGA-COOH in MES, add peptide. Based on general EDC/NHS PLGA protocols (Fischer 2010).

PEG Details: PLGA-PEG-COOH terminus provides carboxyl
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Activate PEG-COOH terminus; react with peptide amine
Conjugation Efficiency (%): PEG spacer improves peptide presentation vs direct PLGA surface
Characterization Method: DLS, BCA, cellular uptake
Key Finding / Notes: PLGA-PEG-COOH activated with EDC/NHS, then peptide-NH2 conjugated. PEG provides flexible tether improving receptor accessibility. Based on standard PLGA-PEG carbodiimide protocols.

PEG Details: Maleimide-PEG-PLGA copolymer; Mal at PEG terminus
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Optimal: maleimide:thiol 2:1 molar ratio
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 84 ± 4% conjugation efficiency at 2:1 Mal:thiol, 30 min, RT, HEPES pH 7.0
Characterization Method: HPLC (cRGDfK quantification), Ellman's (maleimide availability), DLS, zeta, NMR
Key Finding / Notes: KEY REFERENCE for peptide-PLGA Mal-thiol. Comprehensive optimization: tested NP prep method, storage conditions (4°C vs 20°C), Mal:ligand ratios (0.5:1 to 4:1). Best: 2:1 ratio, 30 min, HEPES pH 7.0. Maleimide availability depends on NP prep method — surface maleimide may be lower than expected due to PEG-PLGA miscibility burying some Mal groups.

PEG Details: NPs from 65% PLGA + 20% Mal-PEG-PLGA + 15% Cy5-PLGHMGA blend
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): cRGD:Mal-PEG-PLGA ratios: 1:10 (low), 1:5 (medium), 1:2 (high)
Conjugation Efficiency (%): Conjugation efficiency 40-70% (density-dependent); uptake 2-3× higher under static; significant under physiological flow
Characterization Method: DLS, flow cytometry, epifluorescence + confocal microscopy, static + flow (shear 300 s⁻¹) uptake studies
Key Finding / Notes: Tested cRGD at 3 surface densities on HUVEC endothelial cells under both static and physiological flow conditions (shear rate 300 s⁻¹). Uptake was time-, concentration-, and cRGD density-dependent. Key finding: targeting works under flow conditions relevant to in vivo.

PEG Details: PLA-PEG-MAL orients at oil-water interface during NP formation; Mal on surface
Activation Agent: None (cRGD thiol reacts with surface Mal)
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): PLA-PEG-MAL self-assembles at emulsion interface; maleimide groups face outward for cRGD coupling
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 2-3 fold increased cellular uptake; increased tumor accumulation in vivo (4T1 model, ~2× AUC)
Characterization Method: NMR (maleimide peak disappearance confirms coupling), DLS, in vitro uptake (4T1), in vivo tumor accumulation
Key Finding / Notes: IAASF technique: PLA-PEG-MAL copolymer added during PLGA NP emulsification. PEG-MAL orients at oil-water interface → Mal displayed on NP surface. React with cRGD-SH. NMR confirms coupling (maleimide proton peak disappears). 2-3× uptake increase; ~2× tumor AUC in vivo.

PEG Details: 1 mol% DMG-PEG + 0.5 mol% DSPE-PEG-maleimide in LNP formulation
Molar Ratio (Ligand:NP): Peptide at 1.2-fold molar excess to Mal; 0.5 mol% cRGD optimal for transfection
Incubation Time (h): 2h coupling; quench with free L-cysteine; purify via 30 kDa or 300 kDa centrifugal filters
Conjugation Efficiency (%): 0.5 mol% cRGD showed highest transfection; properties consistent across experiments
Characterization Method: DLS, DiI visualization, mRNA transfection (FLuc), peptide quantification (FAM label)
Key Finding / Notes: Post-conjugation technique (PCT) for LNPs: formulate LNPs with 1% DMG-PEG + 0.5% DSPE-PEG-Mal via microfluidics. Add Cys-peptide in DMF at 1.2× excess. React RT 2h. Quench with free L-Cys. Purify by centrifugal filtration. Tested 5 different peptides (4-31 residues). 0.5 mol% cRGD optimal.
